title: Ivy cloaks the Pullman house's ground storey, as the old photograph shows
items: At 1729 Prairie, the Boston ivy now covers the ground storey of the front south of the portico, and the 18th Street side up to the porte-cochère, in one mantle that stops level under the balcony's belt course. This follows the Detroit Publishing view of about 1900.
The two round-arched front windows stay clear, as in the photograph, and the ivy grows under their sills.
